page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a 32-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server allocates 32 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, translating to a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66296.43 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19774.0. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, registering a top-tier Passmark memory score and a large-block read-only memory bandwidth of 450.77 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, scoring in the top tier of Passmark database benchmarks at 37222.49. However, large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model scoring in the bottom 10% at 4.66 tokens/sec.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-intensive tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage and strong multi-threaded decompression capabilities makes it well-suited for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
